Of special note is the quantity of fixed electronics the Owens carries: a C3 network slave, Beagle active probe, and TAG gear.

With this array, the Owens can find and fix the enemy with indirect fire from supporting elements while the main body moves against the enemy's flank. The Owens rarely engages and destroys the enemy directly; instead, it uses its targeting and communications systems to assist heavier units in performing that task. The seven tons of available pod space allow commanders to tailor the configuration to specific mission requirements.

The Owens has a top speed of 129.6 km/h and is protected with seven tons of armor. The 'Mech's unique mix of speed, armor, and electronic warfare equipment make the Owens a valuable asset in urban and dense woods or jungle environments where it can find an enemy unit that is hidden, designate them for an artillery strike, and then leave the area at high speeds.
BMOwens_OW1Upgraded.notes: Bubbles' Marauders Owens updated for IlClan era.
BMOwens_OW1Upgraded.history:
The DCMS deployed the Owens in 3056, and by the outbreak of the Word of Blake Jihad most frontline regiments could boast between a lance and a company of these versatile machines. The design has proven invaluable for coordinating fire support and providing tactical intelligence to command elements in real-time.

Outside of the Draconis Combine, the Owens also appeared among the ranks of the Com Guards and the reborn Star League Defense Force. During the détente of the Second Star League, most of the other Successor States were able to purchase examples of the design, spreading this capable reconnaissance platform across the Inner Sphere.

Following a reverse-engineered copy of the Black Hawk designated the Black Hawk-KU, the Owens was the next 'Mech in LAW's OmniMech line. The design focused on classic cavalry roles of screening and reconnaissance rather than direct combat, filling a critical gap in DCMS force structure that had previously relied on aging conventional designs.
BMOwens_OW1Upgraded.deployment: The Primary configuration uses small and medium lasers for self-defense while LRM racks on the 'Mech's arms offer suppressive fire in indirect support of other units in the lance or company. This loadout emphasizes the Owens' role as a spotter and support platform rather than a direct combatant, allowing the pilot to focus on maintaining TAG designation and C3 network integrity while contributing modest but sustained firepower to the formation.
BMOwens_OW1Upgraded.manufacturer: Luthien Armor Works (OmniMech Production Facility)|Irian BattleMechs Unlimited

BMRaptor_RTX1OBUpgraded.overview:
The Raptor holds the distinction of being the first Inner Sphere OmniMech ever produced. Designed by Luthien Armor Works as a proof of concept after months of studying Clan OmniMech salvage recovered from the Battle of Luthien in 3052, the twenty-five ton design validated that Inner Sphere engineers could replicate the modular technology that had given the Clans such a decisive advantage during the invasion. The Raptor filled the role of a light reconnaissance and fast strike platform, where its ability to rapidly reconfigure loadouts between missions proved invaluable to Draconis Combine commanders adjusting to the new reality of the Clan threat.

Though initially regarded with skepticism by traditionalists within the DCMS, Luthien Armor Works stood behind the design and eventually won over even its harshest critics. The Raptor became the premier light OmniMech of the Combine, and its prolific production saw it spread beyond Combine borders to become one of the most widely fielded Inner Sphere OmniMechs of its era.
BMRaptor_RTX1OBUpgraded.capabilities:
The Raptor is built on an Alshain Type KR140 endo steel chassis powered by a weight-saving Omni 175 XL engine, giving the design a top speed of just under 119 kilometers per hour. This speed is the Raptor's primary defense, as three and a half tons of StarSlab/4 armor provides only modest protection against sustained fire. The trade-off is deliberate, maximizing the eleven and a half tons of pod space available for mission-specific loadouts, which represents an impressive proportion of the chassis's total mass.

The Prime configuration reflects a versatile combat philosophy, mounting three LRM-5 launchers for long-range harassment alongside two medium lasers and two small lasers for closer engagements. A pair of machine guns provides anti-infantry capability. This mix allows the Prime to contribute meaningfully at multiple range brackets while maintaining the speed to disengage when outmatched.

With seven distinct factory configurations and additional field variants, the Raptor demonstrates the flexibility that makes OmniMech technology so valued. Loadouts range from pure energy builds for extended operations to electronic warfare packages and even an underwater combat configuration, ensuring the Raptor can be tailored to virtually any light 'Mech mission profile.
BMRaptor_RTX1OBUpgraded.notes: Bubbles' Marauders Raptor updated for IlClan era.
BMRaptor_RTX1OBUpgraded.history:
The Raptor's origins trace directly to the Battle of Luthien in January 3052, when the combined defense of the Combine capital against Clan Smoke Jaguar and Clan Nova Cat yielded significant quantities of Clan salvage. Luthien Armor Works engineers studied the captured OmniMech technology intensively, and by May 3052, just months after the battle, the first Raptors walked off the production line at the OmniMech Production Facility on Luthien. The very first units were assigned to the Dragon's Claws for testing, with additional Raptors sent to the Sword of Light, Genyosha, and Ghost regiments for further evaluation.

Acceptance within the DCMS was gradual. Many Combine soldiers, steeped in tradition, were slow to appreciate the advantages of an OmniMech that could swap its weapons between engagements. It took years for the standard Combine soldier to recognize the tactical flexibility the Raptor offered, but its performance during Operation Bulldog in 3059 and the Combine-Dominion War proved decisive in cementing the design's reputation. By the early 3060s, the Raptor was found in the regiments of every top-rated command within the Combine.

The Raptor's success saw it proliferate beyond Combine boundaries, becoming available to allied states and even appearing in mercenary commands. The design's "Easy to Maintain" reputation made it popular with units that lacked dedicated OmniMech maintenance facilities, as the Raptor proved more forgiving of improvised repair work than many of its contemporaries.

Production at Luthien Armor Works continued through the Civil War era, but the facility ceased Raptor production during the Jihad when the Word of Blake's assault on Luthien devastated much of the planet's industrial capacity. While LAW survived and eventually resumed other production lines, Raptor manufacturing was not restarted, leaving surviving units increasingly reliant on salvage and aftermarket parts to remain operational.
BMRaptor_RTX1OBUpgraded.deployment: Alternate Configuration B is purpose-built for close-quarters combat, carrying three SRM-6 launchers backed by a single small laser. This heavy short-range missile load makes the Raptor B particularly effective in a vehicle-hunting role, where its speed allows it to close rapidly and deliver devastating volleys of missiles before withdrawing. The configuration also excels in mop-up operations where surviving enemy forces must be engaged at close range.

BMRaven_RVN3LUpgraded.overview:
The Raven is a thirty-five ton electronic warfare BattleMech developed by the Capellan Confederation, with the first prototype, the RVN-1X, entering service in 3024. Wedged between the Free Worlds League and Federated Suns, the diminutive Confederation was desperately searching for force multipliers at the close of the Third Succession War. One ambitious research program attempted to recreate the sophisticated electronic warfare technology of the long-lost Star League era. While the resulting Ceres Arms Electronic Warfare X-1 equipment was a technical success, the seven-and-a-half ton package proved too bulky to install on any existing BattleMech chassis.

Rather than abandon a promising technology, Chancellor Maximillian Liao directed Hellespont Industries to develop an entirely new design built around the electronics. The resulting Raven was one of the first truly original BattleMech designs produced in centuries, though the prototype would not live up to its ambitious expectations until the recovery of lostech allowed Hellespont 'Mech Works to produce the definitive RVN-3L model in the late 3040s.
BMRaven_RVN3LUpgraded.capabilities:
The production RVN-3L Raven is built around the most comprehensive electronic warfare suite available to any Inner Sphere light 'Mech of its era. The Apple Churchill consortium provides the complete electronics package, including a Guardian ECM suite to blanket friendly units with electronic jamming, a Beagle Active Probe to locate hidden enemies, Target Acquisition Gear for designating artillery targets, and a Narc Missile Beacon to improve allied missile accuracy. A Ceres Metals Model 666 communications system integrates these disparate systems into a cohesive electronic warfare platform.

A Hermes 210 XL engine provides a respectable top speed of ninety-seven kilometers per hour, while four and a half tons of Hellespont Lite ferro-fibrous armor offers reasonable protection for a design never intended to see direct combat. The Raven's offensive armament is deliberately modest, consisting of a Harpoon-6 SRM-6 launcher and a pair of Ceres Arms medium lasers. CASE protection in the left torso mitigates the risk of ammunition explosions.

The Raven's design philosophy accepts that any mission requiring direct engagement is a tactical failure. Its true value lies in electronic countermeasures, target designation, and sensor operations conducted from standoff range. When forced into combat, the 'Mech's light armor and limited firepower make survival dependent on speed and the hope that reinforcements arrive quickly.
BMRaven_RVN3LUpgraded.notes: Bubbles' Marauders Raven updated for IlClan era.
BMRaven_RVN3LUpgraded.history:
The Raven's combat debut came during the Fourth Succession War, when prototype RVN-1X models were pressed into service against the Federated Suns. Deployed at the battalion level as temporary additions to command lances, these early Ravens provided electronic warfare support to Capellan formations, but the primitive EW equipment could not provide a sufficient edge to influence the course of engagements. Many Ravens were captured by Davion forces during the conflict, with some sent to the New Avalon Institute of Science for reverse engineering while others were retained by the units that seized them.

One of the Raven's earliest notable missions involved providing electronic cover for Capellan units participating in Operation Intruders Communion. A pair of Ravens supported a commando team sent to raid a secret NAIS laboratory on Bethel, where they successfully recovered prototypes of a new and powerful type of myomer in exchange for the loss of one Raven. The Capellan Confederation continued to experiment with this triple-strength myomer, incorporating it into the RVN-3X variant despite the technology's dangerous flaws.

The recovery of the Gray Death Core in the 3030s rejuvenated the entire Inner Sphere's technological base, and Hellespont 'Mech Works used the recovered knowledge to finally produce a Raven worthy of its original design ambitions. The RVN-3L entered production in the late 3040s and quickly established itself as the premier electronic warfare platform in the Inner Sphere. While closely associated with House Liao, the Capellan Confederation also exported Ravens to the Free Worlds League and Draconis Combine, with the larger share going to the former. Smaller numbers found their way into Federated Suns and Lyran hands through salvage and battlefield capture.

During Operation Sovereign Justice, Capellan March forces captured a significant number of damaged Ravens. These "Shattered Ravens" were rebuilt and re-armed by Johnston Industries on New Syrtis with weapons configurations significantly different from the Capellan original, tailored to address the infantry threats that had facilitated their capture. The Capellan Confederation continued to advance the design through the Civil War era with stealth armor variants and C3-capable models, cementing the Raven's role as a cornerstone of Capellan electronic warfare doctrine.

By the early 3120s, the Raven had served the Confederation for nearly a century. The introduction of the RVN-5L in 3125, designed to operate alongside the heavier Raven II, demonstrated that Hellespont continued to find relevance in the platform. Incorporating the Raven II's engine and the experimental Raven X's XL gyro, the 5L variant represented the latest evolution of a design that had grown from a desperate gamble into one of the Capellan Confederation's most enduring military assets.
BMRaven_RVN3LUpgraded.deployment: The definitive production model, entering service in the late 3040s after Hellespont 'Mech Works leveraged recovered lostech to fulfill the Raven's original design vision. The 3L replaced the standard engine with a Hermes 210 XL, boosting top speed to nearly one hundred kilometers per hour, and mounted a complete Apple Churchill electronics suite including Guardian ECM, Beagle Active Probe, Narc Missile Beacon, and TAG. Hellespont Lite ferro-fibrous armor and CASE protection rounded out a design that became the benchmark for Inner Sphere electronic warfare BattleMechs.

BMStalker_STK3FBMUpgraded.overview:
The Stalker was introduced in 2594 by Triad Technologies as a heavy assault BattleMech designed to anchor battle lines during the Reunification War. Weighing eighty-five tons and mounting an arsenal capable of engaging targets at every range bracket, the Stalker was built to be a walking weapons platform that could absorb tremendous punishment while steadily advancing on enemy positions. Though among the slowest assault 'Mechs ever fielded, the Stalker compensated with overwhelming firepower and thirteen and a half tons of armor protection.

When Triad Technologies was destroyed during the Succession Wars, production continued uninterrupted thanks to existing lines at Irian BattleMechs Unlimited on Shiro III and Trellshire Heavy Industries on Twycross. This ensured that the Free Worlds League and Lyran Commonwealth maintained the largest concentrations of Stalkers, though the design became so ubiquitous across the Inner Sphere and Periphery that it was a fixture in virtually every major military formation for over four centuries. Triad's original marketing slogan captured the design's essence perfectly: it just keeps coming.
BMStalker_STK3FBMUpgraded.capabilities:
The Stalker's armament is designed around a layered engagement philosophy, increasing its damage output as it closes with the enemy. At long range, twin Jackson B5c LRM-10 launchers provide bombardment capability and allow for indirect fire support. As the range closes, two Magna Mark III large lasers add punishing energy fire from the left and right torsos. At close quarters, four Magna Mark II medium lasers and twin Thunderstroke SRM-6 launchers deliver devastating alpha strikes that can cripple opposing 'Mechs. This staggered weapons profile means a Stalker pilot must carefully manage their fire groups, as attempting to discharge all weapons simultaneously will overwhelm the twenty single heat sinks and risk catastrophic ammunition detonation.

The Stalker's thirteen and a half tons of Valiant Lamellor armor provide excellent protection for an assault 'Mech, though its 54 kph top speed powered by a Strand 255 fusion engine makes it one of the slowest designs in its weight class. The original Spar 3c Tight Band fire-control computer was designed to automatically suggest optimal weapon groupings based on target range, a feature that helped mitigate heat management challenges. By the late Succession Wars era, many surviving Stalkers had lost this system to battle damage and aging, forcing pilots to rely on experience and discipline to avoid overheating. The design's lack of jump jets and limited speed leave it vulnerable to faster opponents able to exploit its flanks, but in a straight fight few 'Mechs can match its sustained firepower.
BMStalker_STK3FBMUpgraded.notes: Bubbles' Marauders Stalker updated for IlClan era.
BMStalker_STK3FBMUpgraded.history:
The Stalker entered service with the Star League Defense Force in 2594 and quickly established itself as a cornerstone of assault lances during the Reunification War. For nearly two centuries it served as a reliable workhorse, its combination of firepower and durability making it a favorite for commanders leading major offensive operations. Stalker pilots developed a reputation for aggressive tactics, including the infamous practice of hiding inside buildings and crashing through walls to ambush passing enemy 'Mechs during urban engagements.

The fall of the Star League and destruction of Triad Technologies during the Succession Wars could have spelled the end of the design, but production at Irian BattleMechs Unlimited and Trellshire Heavy Industries ensured continuous manufacturing. The Free Worlds League and Lyran Commonwealth benefited most from this arrangement, though Stalkers were traded, captured, and salvaged across every Successor State and Periphery nation in such quantities that the design became almost unremarkable. This proliferation had the paradoxical effect of making the Stalker simultaneously feared and taken for granted, ignored until one was encountered in combat, at which point even veteran MechWarriors acknowledged the threat.

The long centuries of combat took their toll on surviving Stalkers. The extreme stress placed on the eighty-five-ton chassis led to widespread structural deterioration, forcing technicians across the Inner Sphere to strip ten to fifteen tons of weaponry from aging frames simply to keep them operational. These lightened variants, while weaker, preserved the Stalker's fundamental toughness and kept otherwise irreplaceable assault 'Mechs in service through the darkest periods of the Succession Wars.

The recovery of Star League technology in the late 3040s prompted Irian to introduce the upgraded STK-5M, which saw action during the Clan Invasion. Though improved, even upgraded Stalkers were severely tested by Clan OmniMechs. The Federated Commonwealth developed its own variant, and the FedCom Civil War spurred both successor states to produce further specialized models. StarCorps Industries on Crofton began producing the Davion-aligned STK-7D, while Defiance Industries on Furillo built the Lyran STK-8S. Irian continued refining the Marik line with the STK-6M. The Stalker's presence in the dueling circuits of Solaris VII further cemented its reputation as a proven and versatile platform.

In the Dark Age era, Irian introduced both the STK-9F Clan-tech retrofit and the entirely redesigned Stalker II, ensuring the venerable chassis line continued to evolve. Across more than five centuries of continuous service, the Stalker has fought in virtually every major conflict in the Inner Sphere, proof of the soundness of Triad Technologies' original design philosophy.
BMStalker_STK3FBMUpgraded.deployment: The original production model introduced in 2594 by Triad Technologies, this variant established the Stalker's layered-engagement doctrine with twin LRM-10 launchers for long range bombardment, paired large lasers for intermediate engagements, and a close-range combination of four medium lasers and two SRM-6 racks. Twenty single heat sinks struggle to manage the full arsenal, requiring disciplined fire group management. The STK-3F served as the backbone of SLDF assault formations for nearly two centuries and remained in continuous production at Irian BattleMechs Unlimited and Trellshire Heavy Industries after Triad Technologies was destroyed during the Succession Wars. It remains the most common Stalker variant encountered across the Inner Sphere and Periphery.
BMStalker_STK3FBMUpgraded.manufacturer: Triad Technologies|Irian BattleMechs Unlimited|Trellshire Heavy Industries

BMSunder_SD1OBUpgraded.overview:
The Sunder is a ninety-ton Inner Sphere OmniMech developed by the Draconis Combine as the assault class component of the DCMS first generation of domestically produced OmniMechs. Introduced in 3056, the design was born from the intensive study of captured Clan Hellbringer and Summoner chassis following the Battle of Luthien in 3052. Draconis Combine engineers at Luthien Armor Works determined the leg assemblies of both progenitor designs could support twenty additional tons of mass, though overcoming catastrophic actuator burnout in prototypes and resolving caustic exhaust fouling from torso-mounted pod bays delayed the Sunder's entry into service, making it among the last of the first-generation DCMS OmniMechs to reach full production.

Though initially a Combine-exclusive design, the Sunder's proven chassis attracted interest from multiple successor states, and licensed production eventually spread the assault OmniMech to militaries across the Inner Sphere. This broad manufacturing base has kept the Sunder in continuous service from the Clan Invasion era through the ilClan period.
BMSunder_SD1OBUpgraded.capabilities:
The Sunder is built around a Hermes 360 XL engine that propels the ninety-ton chassis to a top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour. The bulky engine forced designers to relocate the torso OmniPod bays above the cockpit, an arrangement that contributed to early exhaust fouling problems but provides thirty-six tons of available pod space. Sixteen and a half tons of Mitchell Argon armor give the Sunder respectable protection for an assault 'Mech, while fifteen fixed double heat sinks manage the thermal load across most configurations.

In its Prime configuration, the Sunder is built for devastating close-range engagements. An Autocannon/20 forms the core of its firepower, supported by two large lasers for medium-range engagement, a trio of SRM-4 launchers, and two medium lasers. This loadout makes the Prime variant most lethal at short ranges, though the large lasers provide adequate reach to engage enemies closing on its position.

While thirty-six tons of pod space theoretically make the Sunder a powerful combatant, its reduced ground speed and reliance on less efficient Inner Sphere weaponry leave it at a disadvantage compared to many Clan assault OmniMechs. The widespread use of salvaged Clan OmniPods during Operation Bulldog finally allowed the Sunder to compete on more equal footing with designs such as the Warhawk and Executioner.
BMSunder_SD1OBUpgraded.notes: Bubbles' Marauders Sunder updated for IlClan era.
BMSunder_SD1OBUpgraded.history:
The Sunder's origins lie in the aftermath of the Battle of Luthien in 3052, when Draconis Combine forces captured examples of the Clan Hellbringer and Summoner OmniMechs. Combine engineers at Luthien Armor Works began an ambitious program to reverse-engineer these designs for domestic manufacture, selecting the assault weight class as one of several parallel development efforts alongside the Avatar and other first-generation OmniMechs. Prototype Sunders suffered from catastrophic actuator failure as the heavier chassis overstressed components designed for lighter Clan machines, and additional problems with caustic exhaust residue from torso-mounted weapons fouling the cockpit canopy and sensor arrays required extensive rework before full production could begin in 3056.

Initial deployment saw Sunders assigned to assault lances stationed along the Clan border, where they played a significant role during Operation Bulldog. The DCMS authorization for widespread use of salvaged Clan weaponry in OmniPods proved transformative, as Sunders equipped with Clan-grade weapons could finally compete favorably against Clan Warhawk and Executioner OmniMechs. Many Sunders also served as the anchor point of DCMS command networks, with dedicated C3 configurations enabling lance and company-level coordination that proved its effectiveness during the conflict.

StarCorps Industries recognized the Sunder's potential and licensed production from Luthien Armor Works in the early 3060s, establishing manufacturing lines at their plants on Crofton, Loburg, Son Hoa, and St. Ives. This licensing arrangement proved fortuitous when the Word of Blake Jihad devastated the DCMS's industrial base. Luthien Armor Works' OmniMech production facility was destroyed during the opening stages of the Jihad, cutting off the Combine's primary source of Sunders. StarCorps continued production for the Federated Suns, Lyran Alliance, and Capellan Confederation, ensuring the design survived even as the DCMS lost access to new production.

The Sunder continued to see combat during the tensions surrounding the Lyons Thumb and throughout the First Combine-Dominion War, where its role as a C3 network anchor proved particularly valuable. In the Dark Age era, new configurations incorporating Clan-spec weaponry and advanced electronics such as C3 boosted slave units and TSEMP cannons demonstrated the chassis's continued relevance. StarCorps facilities on Crofton and Loburg maintained production into the ilClan era, keeping the Sunder in service across multiple successor states long after its original Combine-only production had ended.
BMSunder_SD1OBUpgraded.deployment: Alternate Configuration B is purpose-built as a command and control platform, mounting two C3 master computers that enable coordination of up to three full lances of networked 'Mechs. This configuration is intended to deploy and safeguard the central C3 node of an entire company-level formation. An LRM-20 and an LRM-10 provide long-range bombardment capability, while two medium pulse lasers and two medium lasers offer short-range defensive firepower. The heavy reliance on long-range missiles makes this configuration vulnerable to aggressive rushing attacks.
BMSunder_SD1OBUpgraded.manufacturer: Luthien Armor Works - OmniMech Production Facility|StarCorps Industries|StarCorps Industries|StarCorps Industries|StarCorps Industries

BMThanatos_TNS4TUpgraded.overview:
The Thanatos was developed by StarCorps Industries as a seventy-five ton OmniMech intended to emulate the Clan Summoner. After years of producing licensed OmniMechs from Luthien Armor Works on four worlds in the Federated Commonwealth and St. Ives Compact, StarCorps had gained sufficient expertise to design their own Omni-technology platforms by 3060. When neither the LAAF nor the AFFS expressed interest in another OmniMech design, citing high costs and the availability of existing models, StarCorps converted the Thanatos into a standard BattleMech. This pragmatic decision won contracts from both militaries beginning in 3061.

Produced at StarCorps facilities on Crofton and Loburg, the Thanatos filled the role of a heavy cavalry platform, offering a blend of speed, firepower, and electronic warfare capability that kept it in production through the Jihad, Dark Age, and into the ilClan era.
BMThanatos_TNS4TUpgraded.capabilities:
Taking design cues from the Clan Thor, the Thanatos is built on a StarFrame Heavy Endo Steel chassis and powered by a PlasmaStar 375 Extra Light engine, giving it a top speed of 86 kph, fast for a heavy BattleMech. Five Audi-Fokker Mark IV jump jets provide an additional 150 meters of jumping capability. The internal components and electronics systems are heavily reinforced and stabilized, giving the chassis excellent resistance to rough terrain and combat impacts. Thirteen tons of Durallex Heavy armor provide solid protection for its weight class, though the extra-light engine remains a vulnerability if either side torso is breached.

The weapons array is weighted toward medium and short range engagements. A Defiance Model 6 extended-range large laser provides long-range reach, while a Shigunga MRM-20 launcher and two Defiance Model XII extended-range medium lasers deliver punishing firepower at closer ranges. A RAMTech 800P medium pulse laser adds accurate close-range fire. A Guardian ECM suite disrupts enemy electronics, while a C3 slave unit dramatically improves accuracy when operating as part of a networked lance.
BMThanatos_TNS4TUpgraded.notes: Bubbles' Marauders Thanatos updated for IlClan era.
BMThanatos_TNS4TUpgraded.history:
The Thanatos traces its origins to StarCorps Industries' experience producing licensed OmniMechs from Luthien Armor Works. By 3060, StarCorps was manufacturing Black Hawk KUs, Avatars, and Sunders across four worlds, building the institutional knowledge necessary to design their own Omni-technology platforms. The Thanatos emerged alongside the Manteuffel OmniVehicle as the first fruits of this initiative. When neither the LAAF nor the AFFS expressed interest in the OmniMech version, StarCorps converted it into a standard BattleMech, a decision that proved shrewd, winning contracts from both militaries that carried production from 3061 into the next decade.

The Thanatos found its niche in heavy cavalry formations, operating alongside similarly fast designs like the Argus, Barghest, Falconer, and Rakshasa. It displaced aging Quickdraws in units such as the First Federated Suns Armored Cavalry and the Alliance Jaegers. StarCorps also marketed the design to mercenary commands, with buyers ranging from the prestigious Eridani Light Horse to smaller outfits.

Production survived the Jihad at both the Crofton and Loburg facilities. The Jihad era produced the TNS-6T refit, which replaced the original's missile and laser loadout with a snub-nose PPC and multi-missile launcher. Both factories began producing the -6T as a standard model during the 3080s, with Loburg also offering the CASE II-equipped TNS-6S2 subvariant.

During the Dark Age, the Thanatos continued to serve the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns and the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces. In 3146, Republic Armed Forces technicians developed an upgraded variant using Clan-specification weapons during a stopover on Terra. These specifications were passed to StarCorps on Crofton, which began producing the TNS-7D for the AFFS, featuring an all-ClanTech weapons suite that dramatically improved the design's reach and accuracy. StarCorps subsequently offered the TNS-7D2 subvariant, trading electronic warfare capability for an Artemis V fire-control system.

Though some observers considered the Thanatos as never quite fulfilling the potential StarCorps originally envisioned, the design proved durable and adaptable enough to remain in continuous production for nearly a century, evidence of the soundness of its underlying chassis and the flexibility of its weapon bays.
BMThanatos_TNS4TUpgraded.deployment: This variant trades the base model's speed for raw firepower. A lighter engine reduces the top speed to 64 kph, while the extended-range lasers are replaced by four medium pulse lasers. The variant's primary striking power comes from an LB 20-X autocannon mounted in the left arm, capable of firing both solid and cluster munitions. The MRM-20, Guardian ECM suite, and C3 slave are retained, and four jump jets allow 120 meters of jump distance. This variant emphasizes close-range devastation at the cost of the original's speed advantage.

BMVictor_VTR9BUpgraded.overview: The Victor was built in 2508 under contract to the Terran Hegemony as an 80-ton assault 'Mech with an unusual emphasis on mobility. Conceived as a close-range support platform with jump capabilities, the Victor was one of the first assault-weight designs to prioritize maneuverability alongside raw firepower. HildCo Interplanetary and Independence Weaponry produced the design at multiple facilities throughout the Star League era, with the lion's share built for export sale to League member states. Because it served exclusively in line regiments rather than Royal units, the Victor was never outfitted with the advanced technology that would later be lost during the Succession Wars, a fact which ironically ensured its continued maintainability through those dark centuries.
BMVictor_VTR9BUpgraded.capabilities:
The Victor approaches the concept of fire support in an unorthodox manner for a 'Mech of its weight class. Its primary armament is the massive Pontiac 100 autocannon mounted in the right arm, capable of downing most light 'Mechs in a single volley and stripping armor from any location on heavier designs. The left arm carries twin Sorenstein V medium lasers as close-range backup, supplemented by a Holly short-range missile rack in the left torso. Though some early models reported ammunition feed problems with the autocannon, this was never a widespread issue. The original Standus 20 targeting system was replaced early in production with the more reliable MaLandry 34 after the Standus demonstrated a tendency to project false targets.

The Victor's greatest tactical asset is its mobility. While its Pitban engine provides only a modest ground speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, the four HildCo Model 12 jump jets built into the legs and torso allow the Victor to leap into optimal firing positions, seize elevated terrain, or close rapidly with enemies who expect an assault 'Mech to be earthbound. This jump capability can catch inexperienced MechWarriors off guard and proves particularly advantageous in mountainous or urban terrain. The principal sacrifice for this superb mobility is the Victor's relatively thin armor protection of only eleven and a half tons of Durallex Heavy plating, light for an eighty-ton machine and a persistent concern for pilots who find themselves unable to disengage. The lack of dedicated anti-infantry weapons is a secondary weakness, though one addressed by several later variants.
BMVictor_VTR9BUpgraded.notes: Bubbles' Marauders Victor updated for IlClan era.
BMVictor_VTR9BUpgraded.history:
The Victor's origins predate the Star League by over a century and a half, having been manufactured for the Terran Hegemony beginning in 2508. The Star League Defense Force employed the Victor during the Reunification War, where units like the Twenty-Eighth Heavy Horse Regiment used the design to devastating effect. Demand proved high enough that the design was produced at several factories throughout the Star League era, with an estimated one thousand Victors built before the League fell. Many of these departed with Aleksandr Kerensky during the Exodus, and the Clans would later convert captured examples into their own garrison variants. The Twenty-Eighth Heavy Horse would remain behind as mercenaries in Kurita service after the Exodus before their final dissolution during the Second Succession War.

The destruction of all three HildCo Interplanetary Victor production lines during the First Succession War left only Independence Weaponry on Quentin capable of manufacturing new Victors. When the Federated Suns captured Quentin during the Second Succession War, the Victor became the AFFS's primary assault 'Mech and a favored command mount for battalion and regimental commanders. Davion's Avalon Hussars used their Victors to great advantage against House Liao, with the design's jump capability proving decisive in mountainous terrain on Wei and Redfield. The Draconis Combine eventually retook Quentin following the War of 3039, but most Kurita samurai were too proud to adopt a design so closely associated with their traditional enemy. The Federated Commonwealth responded by purchasing new Victors from the rebuilt HildCo factory in the St. Ives Compact and funding the reconstruction of Tao 'Mechworks on Styk to produce the VTR-9D.

The Clan Invasion spurred the development of upgraded Victor models incorporating rediscovered Star League technology. Independence Weaponry had nearly completed prototype work on the VTR-9D when Quentin fell to House Kurita, prompting them to redesign the improved Victor as the VTR-9K for mass production shortly after the Clans invaded. The formation of the Second Star League and destruction of Clan Smoke Jaguar finally won the design acceptance among Combine warriors, with the Ghost Regiments and Legion of Vega receiving the bulk of Independence's output. When the Capellan Confederation recaptured both St. Ives and Styk, the Federated Suns contracted General Motors and the Blackwell Corporation to produce new Victor variants at their New Valencia facility.

Though it had officially fallen out of favor by the FedCom Civil War era, the Victor remained a firm favorite of Allied troops during that conflict. The fall of St. Ives and Styk netted the Capellan Confederation two manufacturing lines, which were modified to produce the stealth-capable VTR-10L. GM/Blackwell continued to develop new variants on New Valencia through the Jihad and into the Dark Age, and when the factory was salvaged after the Jihad, GM put the Victor back into production in the early 3080s. The latest VTR-12D variant shares many components with the Templar III, reflecting General Motors' efforts to streamline their assault 'Mech production lines. The Victor's longevity across more than six centuries of warfare stands as sign of the soundness of its original design philosophy.
BMVictor_VTR9BUpgraded.deployment: The definitive Succession Wars-era Victor, this variant replaced the unpopular 9A after a single production run and became the standard model produced across all Victor factories. Armed with the devastating Pontiac 100 autocannon, twin Sorenstein V medium lasers, and a Holly SRM-4 rack, the 9B established the Victor's reputation as a formidable close-range assault platform. Its combination of jump capability and heavy firepower made it a preferred command mount for battalion and regimental commanders throughout the Federated Suns, and salvaged examples were prized by all Successor States during the resource-scarce Succession Wars era.

BMViking_VKG2FBMUpgraded.overview:
The Viking is a 90-ton assault BattleMech introduced in 3059 as a joint development between ComStar and the Free Rasalhague Republic. Intended to replace the aging Bombardier in the fire support role, the design emerged from Grumium Creations, a small manufacturer on the Republic world of Grumium that ComStar had helped transform into a capable production facility. The Viking represented the second 'Mech co-produced by the two powers, following closely on the heels of the successful Beowulf program.

Built around massive long-range missile batteries guided by advanced fire control systems, the Viking was designed to deliver overwhelming firepower at range. Though its lack of an extralight engine limits its speed, the design's heavy armor and dual CASE ammunition protection give it exceptional staying power on the battlefield. The Viking has seen widespread service, transitioning through several political upheavals alongside its home world of Grumium.
BMViking_VKG2FBMUpgraded.capabilities:
The Viking's primary mission is long-range missile fire support, and its designers built the entire 'Mech around that concept. Four Shigunga missile launchers, a pair of LRM-20s and a pair of LRM-15s, give the design an impressive volume of fire at range. Each launcher is linked to an Artemis IV fire control system for improved accuracy, allowing Viking formations to deliver concentrated and precise missile volleys against hardened targets.

The GC Type 1 Endo Steel chassis saves critical weight while supporting fifteen and a half tons of GC Slab armor, providing excellent protection for an assault 'Mech. Dual CASE systems guard against catastrophic ammunition detonations, a critical feature given the large stores of missile ordnance the design carries. For close defense, two ChisComp 32 small lasers and four SperryBrowning machine guns provide a modest but sufficient deterrent against infantry and light 'Mechs that breach the missile envelope.

The GM 270 engine limits the Viking to a top speed of 54 kilometers per hour, a modest pace for a design of its weight, but adequate for a rear-echelon fire support platform that need not close with the enemy. Ten double heat sinks manage the design's moderate thermal output with ease.
BMViking_VKG2FBMUpgraded.notes: Bubbles' Marauders Viking updated for IlClan era.
BMViking_VKG2FBMUpgraded.history:
The Viking's origins trace to the late 3050s, when ComStar invested heavily in the Free Rasalhague Republic's military manufacturing infrastructure. Grumium Creations, a small parts and systems company on the Republic world of Grumium, was transformed through ComStar financing into a full-scale BattleMech production facility. The Viking was the second design to roll off the upgraded assembly lines, following the lighter Beowulf. ComStar officials had specifically requested a new fire support platform to replace the aging Bombardier, and Grumium obliged by building the Viking around readily available Draconis Combine-sourced Shigunga missile launchers.

Initial production was split between the Com Guards and the KungsArmé, with the Viking appearing in formations such as the 403rd Division and the Third Hussars. The design proved effective in its intended role, capable of delivering punishing volleys of missiles at range while its heavy armor allowed it to absorb return fire that would cripple lighter fire support platforms.

The Jihad brought significant upheaval to the Viking's production history. Grumium fell under Clan Ghost Bear control as the Bears absorbed the remnants of the Free Rasalhague Republic, and the factory continued production under new management. Meanwhile, the Word of Blake captured stockpiles of ComGuard Vikings and refitted them at facilities on Hall, producing the C3i-equipped VKG-3W variant. Loyalist ComGuard forces responded with their own refit program, producing the artillery-focused VKG-3A at the Arcturan Arms facility on Arcturus.

With the formation of the Rasalhague Dominion, the Grumium factory entered a period of declining activity. While the base VKG-2F and assault-oriented VKG-2G continued to see service in Dominion and garrison forces, production at the facility eventually wound down. The Viking nonetheless remains a recognizable fire support platform, with examples serving across multiple successor states and Clan territories well into the thirty-second century.
BMViking_VKG2FBMUpgraded.deployment: The base model serves as the standard production variant, fielding the full complement of four Artemis-guided Shigunga missile launchers alongside backup small lasers and machine guns. Initially split evenly between the Com Guards and the Free Rasalhague Republic's KungsArmé, this variant saw deployment with units such as the Third Hussars and the 403rd Division of the Com Guards. Production continued on Grumium through several changes in planetary sovereignty, from Free Rasalhague Republic to Clan Ghost Bear to the Rasalhague Dominion.

CVVargrAPCTank_BM.overview: The Vargr is a 65-ton wheeled armored personnel carrier developed for the Aurigan Coalition in 2944. Its name derives from the Old Norse word for wolf. Produced on Mechdur, the Coalition's principal industrial world, the Vargr serves as the primary means of moving infantry across contested terrain. Large for its class, it emphasizes protection and carrying capacity over firepower.
CVVargrAPCTank_BM.capabilities:
The Vargr carries a seven-ton infantry bay capable of transporting a full infantry complement to the battlefield. A 240 ICE engine propels the vehicle to 65 km/h on suitable terrain. Its turret mounts two machine guns and two medium lasers, providing adequate suppressive fire once infantry has been delivered to the objective.

Armor protection is substantial for a vehicle of its class, improving the likelihood of delivering its payload intact. The use of an ICE engine, while well-suited to the limited industrial base of the Aurigan Periphery, reduces endurance compared to fusion-powered alternatives. The vehicle's armament is light relative to its mass, reflecting its purpose as a carrier rather than a dedicated combat unit.
CVVargrAPCTank_BM.history:
The Vargr first appeared among forces operating in the Aurigan Reach before being formally documented in House Arano: The Aurigan Coalition. Production was centered on Mechdur, the Coalition's sole significant industrial world during the period.

The vehicle appears exclusively in Aurigan Coalition unit availability lists from the era, absent even from mercenary rosters, indicating that production output was reserved entirely for Coalition forces. Active manufacturing spanned the Late Succession Wars period through the early Renaissance era. The design's tight association with Aurigan Coalition supply chains limited its spread to other factions, and it remains a distinctly regional vehicle.
CVVargrAPCTank_BM.deployment: The base Vargr delivers infantry to contested positions under armor protection across Aurigan Coalition ground operations. Once troops are disembarked, the turret-mounted machine guns and medium lasers allow the vehicle to remain on the battlefield as a fire support platform rather than withdrawing. It serves Coalition forces throughout the Late Succession Wars era.

DSColossus_ColossusBM.overview:
The Colossus is the largest assault DropShip constructed during the Star League era, massing 20,000 tons in a Spheroid configuration. Commissioned by the Star League Defense Force in the mid-twenty-seventh century, the vessel was designed to transport and support an entire combined-arms Regimental Combat Team in a single hull. Mitchell Vehicles Interstellar delivered a design that fulfilled this ambitious requirement, creating a vessel capable of carrying BattleMechs, heavy vehicles, and infantry simultaneously.

Built for durability above all else, the Colossus features numerous redundant systems that make it exceptionally robust and reliable in the field. However, this capability comes at an equally impressive cost, making the vessel too expensive for most military organizations to risk in routine operations.
DSColossus_ColossusBM.capabilities:
The Colossus Mk I carries a full combined-arms regiment: thirty-six BattleMechs, seventy-two heavy vehicles, and twelve infantry platoons, along with over 1,040 tons of cargo for supplies and spare parts. A crew of over one thousand personnel operates the massive vessel and supports the embarked combat forces. The ship's weapons array covers all firing arcs with a diverse mix of armament. The nose mounts two Gauss rifles, an ER large laser, four medium lasers, two PPCs, and two Arrow IV launchers for long-range indirect fire support.

Each broadside carries two batteries of paired PPCs backed by four LRM-20 racks with Artemis IV fire control, two ER large lasers, and eight medium lasers. The aft arc mounts two ER large lasers and four medium lasers for rear defense. Two hundred fifty-five single heat sinks manage the thermal load from this extensive arsenal. Sixty tons of advanced armor provide exceptional protection for a vessel of any size, and the Colossus's design emphasis on redundancy and field repairability means it can sustain significant combat damage and remain operational.
DSColossus_ColossusBM.history:
The Colossus was born from an embarrassing series of SLDF war games in 2651, when five regiments operating in the conquered Periphery territories revealed a critical lack of coordination between different combat arms. The resulting reorganization created the Regimental Combat Teams, fully integrated combined-arms formations that demanded suitable transportation. Mitchell Vehicles Interstellar answered the call with the Colossus, delivering the first hulls in 2660.

At over 700 million Star League dollars per vessel, the Colossus was prohibitively expensive for the SLDF to risk in normal operations. Despite receiving periodic upgrades over the decades, all but a handful of the class were lost during the Amaris Coup, and the SLDF chose to replace them with the smaller and less expensive Excalibur class rather than resume production.

In 3024, Snord's Irregulars discovered a buried Colossus on the Lyran world of Phecda. Though its structural integrity remained sound after centuries underground, the ship was ultimately cannibalized by Lyran forces after the Irregulars salvaged its cargo of BattleMechs and parts. A second Colossus was unearthed on Epsilon Eridani in 3067, sparking a violent contest between mercenary commands. Following the Jihad, Clyde Spaceyards orbiting Firgrove began producing a small number of Colossus-class vessels annually, restoring the design to active production for the first time in centuries.
DSColossus_ColossusBM.deployment: The standard Colossus represents the upgraded production model that succeeded the original Mk I design. Retaining the massive troop capacity that made the class famous, this variant incorporates improvements to its weapons systems and defensive suite developed during the Star League era. Capable of delivering up to nine companies of BattleMechs in a single drop, the standard Colossus remains the largest dedicated BattleMech transport DropShip ever produced. Its sheer lift capacity makes it invaluable for major offensive operations, though its slow thrust profile and enormous size make it dependent on fighter escorts during contested orbital insertions.
